title: Chain of Thought Monitoring Can Fail Even When CoT Is Necessary
abstract: arXiv:2610.18105v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Chain of Thought (CoT) monitoring is used by frontier labs to detect misbehaviour of AI systems. Yet, its reliability remains poorly understood. We attribute this to the lack of a successful organizing principle that leads to generalizable conclusions about monitoring reliability in different regimes. Recent work attributes monitoring failures to the CoT not being necessary for the answer, and argues that CoT becomes monitorable when it is necessary. We show that this binary necessary/not-necessary organizing principle is too coarse by demonstrating that monitoring failures persist even if the CoT is necessary for the answer. In response, we introduce a more fine-grained organizing principle based on a hierarchy of four CoT necessity levels. translated_title: 即使思维链是必要的，思维链监控也可能失败
translated_abstract: 思维链监控被前沿实验室用于检测AI系统的不当行为。然而，其可靠性仍然知之甚少。我们将此归因于缺乏一个成功的组织原则，无法就不同情形下监控的可靠性得出可泛化的结论。近期的研究将监控失败归因于思维链对答案并非必要，并认为当思维链是必要时，它就变得可被监控。我们证明了这种“必要/非必要”的二元组织原则过于粗糙——即使思维链对答案是必要的，监控失败仍会持续存在。作为回应，我们引入了一种更细粒度的组织原则，该原则基于四个思维链必要性等级的层次结构。在此基础上，我们开发了一个通过干预实验来测量最低三个层级的思维链可监控性的框架。我们在这三个层级上都展示了监控失败的现象。
tldr: 论文证明即使思维链对答案是必要的，监控仍可能失败，并提出四级思维链必要性层次结构及基于干预实验的可监控性测量框架。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that CoT monitoring can fail even when CoT is necessary for the answer, introducing a four-level hierarchy of CoT necessity as a finer-grained organizing principle and an intervention-based framework for measuring CoT monitorability.
